3º de Primaria · Inglés

Sports and hobbies

Ficha para imprimir
123456
1

Pregunta de arranquePiensa 30 segundos antes de seguir

En español decimos «jugar al fútbol», «ir a nadar» y «hacer kárate». ¿En inglés se usa siempre el mismo verbo?

Escribe o di en voz alta tu respuesta. Después .

¡No! En inglés hay tres verbos: play para deportes con pelota (play football), go para deportes que acaban en -ing (go swimming) y do para artes marciales y otras actividades (do karate). Es fácil cuando conoces el truco.

2

Aprende15 apartados

Para empezar: The new player

On Monday, a new girl arrives at Leo's school. Her name is Amira and she's from Morocco.

At break time, Leo and his friends play football in the playground. Amira watches them, but she doesn't say anything.

"Do you want to play?" asks Leo.

"Yes, please!" says Amira with a big smile.

Some boys laugh. "Girls can't play football," says Marcos.

But Amira can play very well. She runs fast, she passes the ball to her team and she scores two goals! At the end, Leo's team wins three–one.

"Wow! You're fantastic," says Leo.

"Thank you. I play every Saturday in a club," says Amira. "And I go swimming on Wednesdays."

Marcos looks at his shoes. "Sorry, Amira," he says. "You're a great player. Do you want to be in my team tomorrow?"

"OK!" says Amira. "But you need to pass the ball!"

Everybody laughs. Now Amira has got lots of new friends.

1. Sports

Sports are great for our body and to make friends. Here are some: football (fútbol), basketball (baloncesto), tennis, volleyball, handball (balonmano), swimming (natación), cycling (ciclismo), skating (patinaje), gymnastics (gimnasia) and karate.

Some sports are played in a team (equipo): football, basketball, volleyball. Others are individual: swimming, tennis, gymnastics. En castellano: muchos nombres de deportes vienen del inglés: foot (pie) + ball (pelota) = fútbol.

2. Water and winter sports

Some sports need water, and others need snow or ice (nieve o hielo).

Water sports (deportes acuáticos):

  • swimming (natación): «I go swimming in the pool.»
  • sailing (vela): you need a boat with a sail.
  • surfing (surf): you need a surfboard and big waves (olas).
  • diving (buceo o saltos): you go under the water.
  • water polo: a team game in the pool.
  • canoeing (piragüismo): you use a paddle (remo).

Winter sports (deportes de invierno):

  • skiing (esquí): you need skis and you go down the mountain.
  • snowboarding: you go down the snow on one board.
  • ice skating (patinaje sobre hielo): you need skates.
  • ice hockey: a team game on ice with sticks and a puck.

Look: most of these sports use go + -ing: go swimming, go sailing, go surfing, go skiing, go ice skating.

In Spain, people go skiing in the Pyrenees and in Sierra Nevada, and they go surfing in the north, for example in Cantabria and the Basque Country.

Activity: classify these sports: skiing, sailing, ice hockey, surfing, diving, snowboarding. Which one do you want to try?

3. Play, go or do?

The verb depends on the sport. Play + sports with a ball or games: play football, play tennis, play basketball, play chess. Go + sports ending in -ing: go swimming, go cycling, go skating, go running. Do + martial arts and other activities: do karate, do judo, do gymnastics, do yoga.

Truco: si hay pelota, play; si acaba en -ing, go; y para lo demás, do. Nunca se dice «play swimming» ni «do football».

Vídeo: Sports Song: Do you like sports? · Fun Kids English (YouTube) · 1,4 millones de visualizaciones

4. Hobbies and free time

A hobby is something you do in your free time (tiempo libre) because you enjoy it. Popular hobbies: reading books, drawing and painting, playing the guitar or the piano, dancing, singing, playing video games, cooking, collecting stickers or stones and taking photos.

To talk about hobbies we often use like + -ing: «I like reading comics», «My sister loves dancing». ¿Cuál es tu hobby favorito?

5. Making, collecting and playing

There are many kinds of hobbies. We can put them in groups:

  • Making things (hacer cosas): make models (maquetas), bake cakes (hacer pasteles), knit (tejer), build with blocks, do origami.
  • Collecting (coleccionar): stickers (cromos), shells (conchas), stones, coins (monedas), stamps (sellos), toy cars.
  • Playing (jugar): chess (ajedrez), board games (juegos de mesa), cards (cartas), video games, hide and seek (escondite).
  • Being outside (al aire libre): gardening (jardinería), fishing (pescar), camping, birdwatching (observar pájaros).

To talk about our hobbies we use like / love + -ing: «I love baking cakes with my grandma.» «My brother likes collecting coins.»

We can also say how long: «I collect stickers. I've got two hundred stickers!»

A hobby is good for us: it helps us relax, learn new things and make friends who like the same things.

Activity: ask three classmates «What's your hobby?» and write a sentence for each person.

6. Days of the week

To say when you do your hobbies, you need the days of the week: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.

We use on with days: «I play basketball on Mondays and on Wednesdays.» And at with the weekend: «I go cycling at the weekend.» Ojo: en inglés los días se escriben siempre con mayúscula: Monday, no monday.

7. My activity timetable

Many children do after-school activities (actividades extraescolares). We can show them in a timetable (horario):

  • On Mondays, I have English lessons.
  • On Tuesdays and Thursdays, I go swimming.
  • On Wednesdays, I play the piano.
  • On Fridays, I play with my friends in the park.
  • At the weekend, I play football in a club.

Remember: days of the week always start with a capital letter (mayúscula) in English: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday. In Spanish, they don't: lunes, martes.

We use on with days: on Monday. And at with times: «I go swimming on Tuesdays at five o'clock.»

To ask: «When do you go swimming?» (¿Cuándo…?) – «On Tuesdays and Thursdays.»

It's important to have free time too! Don't do activities every day: you need time to play and rest.

Activity: make your weekly timetable and write five sentences with on.

Vídeo: The 7 Days of the Week Song ♫ 7 Days of the Week ♫ Kids Songs by The Learning Station · TheLearningStation - Kids Songs and Nursery Rhymes (YouTube) · 78,1 millones de visualizaciones

8. What do you do in your free time?

To ask about hobbies, say: What do you do in your free time? Answer with I + activity: «I play the piano and I go swimming.» To ask about a sport: «Do you play tennis?» — «Yes, I do.» / «No, I don't.»

To ask about days: «When do you do karate?» — «On Tuesdays and Thursdays.» En castellano: en español ponemos «los martes»; en inglés es on + día con -s: «on Tuesdays».

9. Sports places and things

Each sport has got its place and its equipment (material). We play football on a pitch (campo), tennis on a court (pista) and we swim in a swimming pool (piscina). We go skating in an ice rink (pista de hielo) and do gymnastics in a gym.

Equipment: a ball, a racket (raqueta), a bike, a helmet (casco), trainers (zapatillas de deporte), goggles (gafas de natación) and a net (red). «For tennis you need a racket and a ball.»

10. Talking about a match

A match (partido) is a game between two teams (equipos) or two players. Here are the key words:

  • player (jugador) and team: «There are eleven players in a football team.»
  • score a goal (marcar un gol) and score a point (un punto, in basketball or tennis).
  • win (ganar): «We win!» – the winner (ganador).
  • lose (perder): «They lose.» – the loser.
  • draw (empatar): «It's a draw: two–two.»
  • referee (árbitro): the person who makes the rules work.
  • fans (aficionados): the people who watch and shout.

To give the score (resultado) we say the numbers: «The score is three–one.» For zero we often say nil in football: «two–nil».

Useful phrases in a match: «Pass the ball!» (¡Pasa el balón!), «Goal!», «Well done!» (¡Bien hecho!), «Good game!» (¡Buen partido!).

Activity: write a short report of a match: the teams, the score and who scores the goals.

Vídeo: Hey-O We Want To Play-O | Kids Sports And Movement Song | Super Simple Songs · Super Simple Songs - Kids Songs (YouTube) · 8,8 millones de visualizaciones

11. Teamwork and fair play

When we do sport we must respect the rules and the other players. That is fair play (juego limpio). Useful phrases: Well done! (¡bien hecho!), Good game! (¡buen partido!), Pass the ball! (¡pasa la pelota!), My turn! (¡me toca!), Your turn! and Let's play together!

Win or lose, shake hands at the end and say «Good game!». A good player helps the team: We win together, we lose together. Ganar es bonito, pero divertirse y respetar es lo más importante.

12. The Olympic and Paralympic Games

The Olympic Games (Juegos Olímpicos) are the biggest sports competition in the world. They take place every four years, in a different city each time.

  • The Olympic flag has five rings (anillos) of different colours: blue, yellow, black, green and red. They show that people from all the continents come together.
  • There are Summer Games (athletics, swimming, gymnastics…) and Winter Games (skiing, ice skating…).
  • The best athletes win medals: gold (oro) for first, silver (plata) for second and bronze (bronce) for third.

After the Olympic Games come the Paralympic Games (Juegos Paralímpicos). Here, athletes with a disability (discapacidad) compete: some use a wheelchair (silla de ruedas), some can't see, and some have got a prosthetic leg (pierna ortopédica). They are amazing athletes!

The Olympic Games started in ancient Greece, more than 2,700 years ago. In 1992, they took place in Barcelona.

Activity: draw the five Olympic rings and write the names of three Olympic sports.

13. Reading: Jake's week

Read Jake's timetable of activities: «I love sport! On Mondays I play basketball with my school team. On Wednesdays I go swimming at the sports centre. On Fridays I do judo. At the weekend I go cycling with my mum. I don't play football, but I watch it on TV with my grandpa. I've also got a quiet hobby: I collect stamps from other countries!»

Answer: When does Jake go swimming? Does he play football? What does he collect?

14. Let's practise: a class survey

Make a survey. Write five activities in a table: play football, go swimming, do karate, play the piano, read comics. Ask ten classmates: «Do you play football?» «Do you go swimming?» Tick the answers.

Then make a bar chart and say the results: «Seven children play football. Three children do karate. Nobody plays the piano!» ¿Cuál es la actividad más popular de tu clase?

15. Join our club!

Clubs want new members. Let's write a poster (cartel) to invite children to a club. A good poster answers these questions:

  • What? The name of the club: «The Star Chess Club».
  • When? «On Tuesdays at half past five.»
  • Where? «In the school library.»
  • Who? «For children from 7 to 10 years old.»
  • What do you need? «Bring a pencil and a notebook.»

Look at this example:

Do you like dancing? Can you move to the music? Come to the HAPPY FEET DANCE CLUB! When: on Mondays and Wednesdays at five o'clock. Where: in the school gym. Bring comfortable clothes and water. It's free! Come and have fun!

Tips for a good poster:

  • Start with a question to the reader.
  • Write the club name in big letters.
  • Use imperatives (órdenes): Come! Bring! Join us!
  • Add colours and a drawing.

Activity: invent a club and make a poster in English.

Lo hacemos juntos

¿Play, go o do? «___ cycling».

  1. Cycling acaba en -ing.
  2. Con -ing se usa go.

Resultado: go cycling.

Traduce: «Juego al tenis los sábados».

  1. Tenis con pelota: play.
  2. Los sábados = on Saturdays.

Resultado: I play tennis on Saturdays.

Pregunta a un amigo qué hace en su tiempo libre.

  1. Tiempo libre = free time.
  2. Pregunta con What do you do…?

Resultado: What do you do in your free time?

Write the score: we have two goals and they have zero (football).

  1. In football we often say nil for zero.
  2. Say our score first.

Resultado: It's two–nil. We win!

Correct: «I play skiing on saturday.»

  1. Skiing uses go.
  2. Days start with a capital letter and use on.

Resultado: I go skiing on Saturday.

Errores típicos

  • Usar play con todo: «play swimming» → «go swimming».
  • Decir «do football» → «play football».
  • Escribir los días con minúscula: «monday» → «Monday».
  • Usar in con los días: «in Monday» → «on Monday».
  • Olvidar el -ing con go: «go swim» → «go swimming».
  • Writing days of the week with a small letter: «on monday».
  • Confusing win and lose, or saying «play skiing» instead of «go skiing».

Ejercicios (24)

Hazlos en tu cuaderno y después abre la solución.

Nivel básico

  1. Traduce: baloncesto, natación, ciclismo.

    Ver solución
    basketball, swimming, cycling.

  2. ¿Play, go o do? karate, football, skating.

    Ver solución
    do karate, play football, go skating.

  3. Escribe los días del fin de semana.

    Ver solución
    Saturday and Sunday.

  4. Name two water sports.

    Ver solución
    Example: swimming and surfing.

  5. How do you say «ganar» in English?

    Ver solución
    Win.

  6. What colour is the medal for first place?

    Ver solución
    Gold.

  7. In the reading, where is Amira from?

    Ver solución
    From Morocco.

  8. Complete: «I go swimming ___ Tuesdays.»

    Ver solución
    On.

Nivel medio

  1. Completa: «I play the piano ___ Fridays.»

    Ver solución
    on.

  2. Completa: «We go cycling ___ the weekend.»

    Ver solución
    at.

  3. ¿Qué es un hobby?

    Ver solución
    Una actividad que haces en tu tiempo libre porque te gusta.

  4. ¿Dónde se juega al tenis?

    Ver solución
    On a tennis court.

  5. ¿Qué dices al final de un partido?

    Ver solución
    Good game! / Well done!

  6. What does Marcos say about girls?

    Ver solución
    He says that girls can't play football.

  7. Make a question: When / you / go / skiing?

    Ver solución
    When do you go skiing?

  8. Translate: Colecciono conchas.

    Ver solución
    I collect shells.

  9. How often are the Olympic Games?

    Ver solución
    Every four years.

  10. Write the score of a draw with two goals each.

    Ver solución
    Two–two. It's a draw.

Nivel avanzado

  1. Contesta: «Do you play football?» (no)

    Ver solución
    No, I don't.

  2. Escribe dos frases sobre tus aficiones con días.

    Ver solución
    Model answer: I go swimming on Tuesdays. I play video games at the weekend.

  3. What is the message of «The new player»?

    Ver solución
    Girls and boys can play sport; we must be fair and include everybody.

  4. Write a report of a match with the teams, the score and the scorers.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  5. Write your weekly activity timetable with five sentences.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

  6. Make a poster for a club with what, when, where and what to bring.

    Ver solución
    Open answer.

Explícalo con tus palabrasComo si se lo contaras a alguien de un curso menor

¿Has nombrado estas ideas?
★

Situación de aprendizajeOur class sports day

The class organises a small sports day with team games, writes the rules and reports the results in English.

Pasos

  1. Choose four games and make mixed teams.
  2. Write the rules and a timetable for the day.
  3. Play the games and write down the scores.
  4. Write a report with the scores and give a fair play award.

Producto final: A sports day poster and a report with the results in English.

Cómo se valora

  • Uses play, go and do with sports correctly.
  • Uses on with days and at with times.
  • Talks about a match with win, lose, draw and score.
  • Shows teamwork and fair play.

Tarjetas de repasoToca la tarjeta para darle la vuelta

Según cómo respondas, la tarjeta vuelve mañana, en 3, en 7 o en 21 días.

Para familias

  • Haced juntos un horario semanal en inglés con las actividades de cada miembro de la familia.
  • Al ver deporte en la tele, nombrad en inglés el deporte y el material que usan.
  • Repasad juntos las tarjetas del paso 6 dos minutos al día durante una semana.

Para profesores

Saberes: Léxico de deportes y aficiones, colocaciones play / go / do, días de la semana con on, preguntas sobre el tiempo libre (Lengua Extranjera: Inglés) (RD 157/2022, segundo ciclo de Primaria, 3.er curso).

  • Encuesta de deportes con gráfico de barras.
  • Horario semanal de actividades en inglés.
  • Mímica de deportes con la regla play / go / do.

Qué vas a aprender

  • Name sports and free-time activities
  • Use play, go and do correctly with sports
  • Talk about the days you do your hobbies: on Mondays, at the weekend
  • Ask and answer «What do you do in your free time?»
  • Name water and winter sports
  • Talk about a match with win, lose, score and team
  • Learn about the Olympic and Paralympic Games
  • Write a poster to invite people to a club

Palabras clave

sport · hobby · free time · play football · go swimming · do karate · on Mondays · at the weekend · team · ball · practise

Tiempo

80 minutos hoy + 2 minutos en cada repaso
